title: Cap. V Obj. 2: actual gift of eternal life bound to believers — therefore election from foresight faith
latin: Obj. 2. Actualis vitae aeternae datio non magis est adstricta quam ejusdem dandae volitio: Sed ipsa datio adstricta est ad fideles, et fidem antecedentem praesupponit: Ergo et volitio dandae vitae aeternae, quae nihil aliud est quam electio. Electio itaque est ex fide praevisa. Arminius quique Arminium sectantur fere omnes ex hoc principio multa exstruunt argumenta, sed caduca et invalida.
pass_a: Objection 2. The actual gift of eternal life is not more bound than the volition of giving the same: But the gift itself is bound to the faithful, and presupposes antecedent faith: Therefore also the volition of giving eternal life, which is nothing other than election. Election therefore is from foresight faith. Arminius and almost all who follow Arminius build many arguments from this principle, but frail and invalid.
pass_b: Obj. 2. The actual gift of eternal life is no more bound than the will to give it. But the gift itself is bound to the faithful and presupposes antecedent faith. Therefore the will to give eternal life — which is nothing other than election — is likewise bound. So election is from foresight faith. Arminius and almost all who follow him build many arguments from this principle — frail and invalid.

title: Cap. V Obj. 2 Sol: more required as instruments for external work than as motives for intention
latin: Sol. Docet enim sana Philosophia, plura requiri tanquam instrumenta praecedanea ad productionem alicujus operis in actu externo, quam requiruntur tanquam antecedanea motiva ad intentionem sive destinationem ejusdem in mente et voluntate operantis. Fac enim me velle ita argumentari: Actualis domus alicujus aedificatio non magis est adstricta, quam ejusdem aedificandae volitio: Sed ipsa aedificatio adstricta est ad praecedaneam coaptationem lignorum et lapidum: Ergo ipsa volitio adstricta est ad haec omnia tanquam antecedanea, et ex illorum praevisione nascitur. Inepta sane conclusio.
pass_a: Solution. For sound Philosophy teaches that more things are required as antecedent instruments for the production of some work in an external act, than are required as antecedent motives for the intention or destination of the same in the mind and will of the one operating. For let me wish to argue thus: The actual building of some house is not more bound than the volition of building the same: But the building itself is bound to the antecedent fitting-together of timbers and stones: Therefore the volition itself is bound to all these as antecedents, and is born from foresight of them. A conclusion inept indeed.
pass_b: Sol. Sound philosophy teaches that more is required as antecedent instruments to produce a work in an external act than as antecedent motives for intending or destinating that work in the operator's mind and will. Argue parallel: the actual building of a house is no more bound than the will to build it; but building is bound to the prior fitting of timbers and stones; therefore the will is bound to all those as antecedents and is born from foresight of them. An inept conclusion indeed.

title: Cap. V Obj. 2 Sol: will to build precedes coaptation; eternal life given vs destinated
latin: Non enim ex praevisa coaptatione lapidum et lignorum nascebatur prima voluntas aedificandi in mente artificis; sed vice versa, ex voluntate aedificandi sequebatur illa prima lapidum et lignorum coagmentatio. Pari ratione, vita aeterna in effectu externo producta, et Petro aut Paulo collata, multa praesupponit quae vita aeterna ut in arcana Dei voluntate illis destinata non praerequirit. Destinare ad vitam, est actus immanens in mente Dei; dare vitam vel perducere ad vitam, est opus ad extra tendens in creaturam: illud perficitur et absolvitur solo actu voluntatis Divinae; hoc non perficitur nisi intervenientibus multis creaturae actionibus ex ordinatione Divina praerequisitis.
pass_a: For the first will of building in the mind of the craftsman was not born from foresight of the fitting-together of stones and timbers; but the other way round, from the will of building followed that first joining of stones and timbers. By like reason, eternal life produced in an external effect, and conferred on Peter or Paul, presupposes many things which eternal life as destinated to them in the secret will of God does not prerequire. To destinate to life is an immanent act in the mind of God; to give life or to lead through to life is a work tending outward upon the creature: the former is perfected and completed by the sole act of the Divine will; the latter is not perfected except with many actions of the creature intervening, prerequired by Divine ordination.
pass_b: The craftsman's first will to build was not born from foresight of fitting stones and timbers — the reverse: from the will to build followed that first joining of stones and timbers. Likewise eternal life produced outwardly and conferred on Peter or Paul presupposes many things that eternal life as destinated to them in God's secret will does not prerequire. To destinate to life is an immanent act in God's mind; to give life or lead to life is a work tending outward on the creature. The former is finished by the sole act of the divine will; the latter is not finished without many creaturely actions intervening, prerequired by divine ordination.

lemmas.gloss: eternal life conferred on Peter or Paul

title: Cap. V Obj. 2 Sol close: crass error — God never bound himself Si prius credideris, licebit praedestinare
latin: Crassus igitur error est opinari, primam illam et aeternam personae alicujus singularis a Deo ad vitam destinationem iisdem legibus adstrictam, quibus temporalis consecutio quoad ipsos homines adstricta est. Idem enim Deus qui homini hanc legem dixit, Si credideris, dabo tibi vitam, vel salvus eris, nunquam hanc legem sibi imposuit, Si prius credideris, licebit mihi te praedestinare ad vitam; secus haud licebit.
pass_a: It is therefore a crass error to opine that that first and eternal destination of some singular person by God to life is bound by the same laws by which the temporal attainment as to the men themselves is bound. For the same God who said this law to man, If you shall have believed, I will give you life, or you will be saved, never imposed this law on himself, If you shall first have believed, it will be lawful for me to predestinate you to life; otherwise it will by no means be lawful.
pass_b: So it is a crass error to think that God's first eternal destinating of a singular person to life is bound by the same laws that bind temporal attainment on the human side. The same God who told man, If you believe, I will give you life — or you will be saved — never bound himself: If you first believe, then I may predestinate you to life; otherwise I may not.
